title: Make It Stick: The Science of Successful Learning
author: Peter C. Brown
Henry L. Roediger III
Mark A. McDaniel
target_audience: Educators and teachers at all levels
Anyone interested in neuroscience or psychology of learning
core_themes: How people actually learn versus how they believe they learn
The science behind memory formation and retention
Practical, evidence-based strategies to enhance learning
Overcoming challenges and setbacks in mastering new material
primary_purpose: To bridge scientific research on memory and learning with practical techniques so learners and teachers can adopt more effective, enduring study and teaching strategies that really work.

structure_format.narrative_style: Engaging, accessible, and anecdotal, blending storytelling with scientific research
structure_format.organization: Divided into thematic chapters, each focused on a core scientific concept and its real-life application
features: Case studies and examples from classrooms, sports, medicine, and more
Summaries and quick tips at chapter ends
Illustrations of common learning errors and their remedies

key_concepts_lessons: Retrieval practice—actively recalling information—boosts long-term retention far more than passive review.
Spaced repetition is more effective than cramming for durable learning.
Interleaving (mixing types of material or skills) improves understanding and transfer—though it may feel harder.
Making mistakes and correcting them is a powerful way to learn.
Reflection, elaboration, and self-testing enhance the integration and application of knowledge.
Learning is often counterintuitive: strategies that feel easy or familiar are often the least effective.
Adopting a growth mindset and embracing difficulties improves mastery.
notable_features: Grounded in decades of cognitive psychology research
Breaks down myths such as rereading and highlighting as effective learning methods
Applicability spans K-12, university, professional training, and self-directed learning
Real-world success stories highlight practical impact
cultural_historical_context: Published during a rising interest in evidence-based education, 'Make It Stick' contributed to a broader educational shift away from intuition-based study habits toward scientifically validated methods, in the context of growing research on cognitive science and its classroom applications.
reception_impact: Widely acclaimed in educational, academic, and business circles
Recommended by professional organizations and teachers’ groups
Praised for making cognitive science practical and readable
Influential in teacher-training curriculums and professional development
Has become a staple resource for those revamping study and teaching strategies
comparable_titles: Why Don’t Students Like School? by Daniel T. Willingham
How We Learn by Benedict Carey
Powerful Teaching: Unleash the Science of Learning by Pooja K. Agarwal & Patrice M. Bain
